title: Forest Ecosystems, B.S. — Biodiversity and Conservation Option (College of Agricultural Sciences)
notes: Biodiversity and Conservation Option, University Park (of four: Biodiversity and Conservation, Forest Management, Forests/Trees/People, Watershed Ecohydrology -- Biodiversity and Conservation chosen for the fewest ambiguous multi-department cross-listed pools, e.g. the others reference LARCH/ARCH/RPTM/GEOG courses not yet in any catalog). Major code FORES avoids colliding with the FOR department prefix. Extended the FOR department catalog (started for Wildlife and Fisheries Science with FOR 203/350) with FOR 200/204/255/266/308/409/410/421/430/450W, and hort_catalog.json with HORT 445, sourced from PSU course description pages. Real bug caught during verification: the Semester 1 math item was originally listed as 'MATH 110 (or 140)', causing MATH 110 to be picked -- but CHEM 110's concurrent requirement only recognizes MATH 140/141/22, not MATH 110, cascading into a 3-course warning (CHEM 110/111/202 all stuck) -- reordered to list MATH 140 first, same fix pattern as Earth Science and Policy and Food Science earlier this session. FOR 410 and FOR 450W have unenforceable meta-prereqs ('7th-semester standing', '6 credits of social/behavioral gen-ed') the planner schema doesn't model directly, same limitation as ABSM/TURF's semester-standing courses. The bulletin's 'ENT 313/FOR 403/PPEM 318' pool appears twice (Semester 6 and Semester 8) -- resolved to two distinct courses (ENT 313, then PPEM 318) to avoid scheduling the same code twice. 'Supporting Course' and generic 'Elective' pools are modeled generically, same convention as CMPSC's own open pools. Post-scraper-fix repair: CHEM 110's real prereq is MATH 22 and STAT 200/240/250's real prereq is MATH 21, neither of which were in this plan at all -- and MATH 22/21 themselves real-chain through MATH 4 and MATH 3, also missing. Added all four (MATH 3, MATH 4, MATH 21, MATH 22); confirmed clean (no warnings, goal met) after the addition -- this plan's existing 17cr/semester cap already had enough room to absorb the extra 12cr without needing any further adjustment.
